envelope.text: ADOPT-BOUNDED: `support` is checked to be initialised and otherwise unused.

why: ADOPTED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 C4b): both blockers below are gone. (2) The callback binding site now exists -- `rclc_executor_add_action_server` binds rclc's goal and cancel callbacks -- so the callback-less init is exactly rclc's. (1) `support` is no longer inert: it is CHECKED (`RCL_RET_NOT_INIT` for a support that was never initialised), which is the one fact rclc's reading of it implies; its clock is not used, because the executor's clock times the server. ENVELOPE (stated on the declaration). A NULL `support` is ACCEPTED (phase-515 C4c), as `rclc_timer_init_default` accepts one: a C component the generated entry hosts has no support to pass, and the C action-server components migrate to this constructor. That widens rclc's domain without changing any call rclc accepts. Test: `packages/api/nros-c/tests/run/rclc_action_server.c`. PRIOR ROW: rclc's default-QoS action-server constructor. phase-417 W5.d adopted its SIBLING (`rclc_action_client_init_default`, a `static inline` in <rclc/action.h>) and refused this one, so the old `see `c:action_client_init_default`` no longer carries a reason and the reason is recorded here. TWO things block it, and neither is the QoS. (1) The `support` PARAMETER. rclc takes `rclc_support_t *` in slot 3 and reads it for exactly one thing -- it passes `&support->clock` to `rcl_action_server_init` (`rclc/src/rclc/action_server.c` @ `10eadcc`). `rcl_action_server_init` stores metadata and defers RMW entity creation to `rclc_executor_add_action_server`, so it takes neither a clock nor a support handle: a five-argument forwarder would carry an argument it IGNORES, which is the inert-parameter defect RFC-0089 exists to end and the same refusal `rcl_node_resolve_name` makes for rcl's `allocator` and `is_service`. (2) The CALLBACK BINDING SITE. rclc registers goal and cancel handlers at `rclc_executor_add_action_server`; ours are bound at init. Forwarding to the callback-free `nros_action_server_init_polling` instead would compile and then dispatch nothing -- a plausible name over an opposite data contract. Closing this needs the executor-side binding site, not a wrapper. `absent` rather than `refuse-loud`: nothing declares the name, so a ported file gets `undeclared identifier` (the disposition read `adopt` until W5.d, which described a state that had never existed).
